name: BS 546 5 A
description: British round-pin plug and socket-outlet, 5 A size of BS 546: three round pins in a triangle, a larger earth pin above line and neutral. Superseded by BS 1363 for general UK use; still used in South Asia and parts of Africa, and in the UK for switched lighting circuits.

standards.title: Specification. Two-pole and earthing-pin plugs, socket-outlets and socket-outlet adaptors

standards.scope: Indian 6 A version of the 5 A BS 546 plug (cited by secondary sources)

standards.title: Plugs and socket-outlets for domestic and similar general use standardized in member countries of IEC
standards.scope: Catalogue of national plug and socket-outlet systems

relations.note: BS 1363 replaced BS 546 sockets in new UK installations from 1947; BS 546 remains in use elsewhere.

variants.name: BS 546 5 A plug
variants.keying: The larger earth pin enforces polarity.
mechanicalNotes: Line and neutral pins 5.1 mm in diameter, 14.9 mm long (15.9 mm in the original standard), 19.1 mm between centres.
Earth pin 7.1 mm in diameter, 20.6 mm long, 22.2 mm from the line-neutral axis.

variants.name: BS 546 5 A socket-outlet
variants.keying: Larger earth hole above the line and neutral holes.
mechanicalNotes: Seen from the front with the earth hole at the top: neutral on the left, line on the right.
Sockets are not recessed; in the UK they are only permitted with shutters.

electricalProfiles.name: AC single-phase
conditions: The rating comes from secondary sources; the BS 546 text was not reviewed. The 250 V limit is stated for the whole BS 546 family.
The Indian IS 1293 version of the same plug is rated 6 A; WorldStandards gives 6 A for type D.

ocpi-2.2.1.note: OCPI describes DOMESTIC_D only as a 3-pin type D plug; type D also covers the Indian 6 A IS 1293 version.

notes: Ratings and dimensions rely on secondary sources; the BS 546 text was not reviewed.
Source conflict on the current rating: Wikipedia gives 5 A for the BS 546 size, WorldStandards gives 6 A for type D (the IS 1293 value). The profile records 5 A.
Status conflict: the BSI record lists BS 546:1950 as current, while some resellers list it as superseded or withdrawn.
Frequency is not stated by the cited sources.
The line and neutral positions of the socket face rely on a single secondary source (Wikipedia); the dimensions are confirmed by a second one.
The plug face is not drawn: no reviewed source depicts it separately.
The 2 A, 15 A and 30 A sizes of BS 546 and the IS 1293 6 A version are not modelled.
